tasks.short: Organize space for study equipment and supplies.

steps.what: Read which study visit this room is for
Look up stored equipment and supplies for this visit
Decide how this space should hold the supplies
Organize the space and place the study equipment
Note a missing study supply in the visit record

tasks.design: The {DOCS} study file already lists the equipment and supplies for each visit. A configured lookup opens that visit's list. She still decides how the space should hold the items and places them herself.
tasks.previous_blocker: The kit list sat in a long protocol, and the room layout depended on what was already on the benches.
tasks.enabler_now: The visit's equipment lines can be filtered when they are already stored as a list.
tasks.still_hard: Fitting bulky devices around a subject chair cannot be done from a list.
tasks.human_edge: She sees that a trolley blocks the emergency exit and moves the equipment.
tasks.altitude: Her week still includes setting the room. She only skips hunting the right visit list.

reach.task: Stock the visit kit before the coordinator arrives
reach.learn: Which protocol items must be in the room, and which cupboard holds them

evidence.claim: Opening the visit's stored kit list does not place equipment. The room layout and the physical move stay with the coordinator. Model knowledge.

assumptions: The protocol author already wrote the visit's equipment and supplies as a list in the study file. If that list is only a paper page, the lookup does not run and she reads the page herself.
The study nurse keeps the cupboard location list. That upkeep is her hours, not the coordinator's, so focal incremental hours are 0.
Placing items is physical and stays at full time. The shortage note is written in the same study record, so it is not a second entry.
unknowns: Whether this site stores the visit kit list as fields or only as a scanned page in the binder.
research_questions: Is the visit kit list stored as fields, or only as a scanned page?

already_counted.description: Reading the visit name, choosing the layout, placing the equipment, and noting a shortage stay in her remaining time.

incremental.description: The study nurse keeps the cupboard location list when a kit moves.
The coordinator does not keep that location list.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: A visit with three familiar items makes the list hunt a small part, near 3. A protocol with many visit types can reach 8. Placing the items stays hers either way.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Develop advertising and informational materials for subject recruitment.

steps.what: Read the approved wording for this study recruitment
Decide which informational materials this recruitment needs
Draft the advertising materials from the approved wording

loop.input: Ethics-approved recruitment sentences and the study contact fields
loop.output: A draft advertising paragraph for this material
loop.check: Each sentence is matched to the same claim in the approved wording, not to an identifier. A sentence with no matching claim is flagged and left unchanged.
loop.stop: Stop after one pass, when every sentence is matched or flagged. Flagged sentences are not rewritten.
loop.why_not_simpler: A field copy can place the study name and the contact line. It cannot write the paragraph, because the allowed claims are prose.

steps.what: Develop the final informational wording she will send
Send the approved advertising for subject recruitment

tasks.design: A bounded draft on {DOCS} writes advertising materials from the ethics-approved sentences. She checks every claim and develops the final wording. She then sends that exact version. The draft does not add a claim and does not send itself.
tasks.previous_blocker: The allowed claims were prose in an ethics file, so a template could not write the paragraph.
tasks.enabler_now: A bounded draft can propose sentences and flag any claim that is not in the approved wording.
tasks.still_hard: A new audience whose claims are not in the ethics text still needs a new approval outside this task.
tasks.human_edge: She rejects a sentence that sounds allowed but changes who may take part.
tasks.altitude: She still decides which material is needed and still checks every claim before it leaves. The first draft of wording that is already approved is no longer blank-page work.

reach.learn: Which sentences may appear in a material, and which claims are closed

evidence.claim: A field copy can place a study name and a contact line. It cannot write a paragraph from approved prose, and a person still has to check that each claim is the one the ethics text allows. Model knowledge.
A model-drafted report cited non-existent sources and a fabricated court case, and the firm agreed to repay the final instalment.

assumptions: The investigator already holds the ethics-approved sentences in the study file. The coordinator does not maintain that sentence list, so focal incremental hours are 0.

The draft step finishes without a gate. She checks the meaning in the next step and may rewrite a flagged sentence. The send uses only the text she left in that check. Any later edit voids the approval.
A sentence that is not in the approved wording is not sent. Taking it back to the ethics committee is outside this task.
unknowns: Whether the ethics committee must see each new layout even when every sentence is already approved.
research_questions: Must each new layout go back to the ethics committee when every sentence is already approved?

already_counted.description: Reading the approved wording, choosing the material, correcting the draft, and sending it stay in her remaining time.

incremental.description: The investigator keeps the list of which approved sentences may be reused in which material.
The coordinator does not keep that sentence list.

approvals.approved_version: Advertising text as she left it in s4, each claim checked against the ethics-approved sentences. Any later edit voids this approval.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: A one-line poster has little prose to draft, so the saving stays near 10. A long letter can reach 22. She still rewrites flagged sentences, so it stays under the full drafting share.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Dispense devices or drugs, calculate dosages, and instruct.

steps.what: Read the prescription for this subject's medical visit
Look up the stored strength for these drugs
Calculate the dosages for this subject
Dispense the medical devices or drugs to the subject
Provide instructions for the device or drug

tasks.design: A configured lookup on the {OTHER} clinical study record shows the stored strength and route. She still calculates the dosage, dispenses the drug or device, and instructs the subject. The lookup does not set the dose.
tasks.previous_blocker: Strength and route were fields on a long prescription, and the dose itself depends on this subject.
tasks.enabler_now: Those stored fields can be shown without anyone recalculating the dose.
tasks.still_hard: Weight, renal function, and what the subject last took still change the figure she accepts.
tasks.human_edge: She stops when the strength on screen does not match the product in her hand.
tasks.altitude: Nothing changes in how she calculates, dispenses, or instructs. She only skips scanning the prescription for the strength field.

reach.task: Check a calculated dose before a high-risk handover
reach.learn: Which prescription field holds strength and route, and when the lookup did not run

evidence.claim: Showing a stored strength and route does not calculate a dose. The arithmetic and the decision to hand the product to the subject stay with the person who dispenses. Model knowledge.

assumptions: {OTHER} means the clinical study record. The investigator enters drug, strength, and route before the visit. If strength is only in a scanned note, the lookup does not run.
The investigator keeps the map of which fields hold strength and route. The coordinator does not, so focal incremental hours are 0.

The lookup only shows the stored strength. She calculates the dosage herself. Handing the dose and explaining it happen in the room. They are not a document sent out, so they have no release gate. The prescription she read is the investigator's existing order.
unknowns: Whether this coordinator is allowed to dispense, or a pharmacist must hand over the drug.
research_questions: Is this coordinator allowed to dispense, or must a pharmacist hand over the drug?

already_counted.description: Reading the prescription, calculating the dosage, dispensing, and instructing the subject stay in her remaining time.

incremental.description: The investigator keeps the field map of strength and route.
The coordinator does not keep that field map.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: One familiar drug is a short lookup, near 3. A visit with several drugs can reach 7. The calculation, the dispense, and the instructions stay hers.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Arrange research study sites and check staff or equipment availability.

steps.what: Read which research study sites this protocol names
Look up staff availability on the stored calendars
Determine whether equipment is free at the sites
Arrange the research study site with the site lead
Record the arranged dates on the study file

tasks.design: A configured free or busy view on {CALENDAR} shows which named staff are free on the visit dates. She still determines whether equipment is free and arranges the research study site with the site lead. The view does not assign anyone.
tasks.previous_blocker: She opened each person's calendar, and equipment sat on a separate booking list.
tasks.enabler_now: Free or busy for the roles she already checks can be shown in one view.
tasks.still_hard: A person can be free on the calendar and still be the wrong skill for that visit.
tasks.human_edge: She hears that the site lead will be in clinic and picks another date.
tasks.altitude: She still chooses the site and the date. She no longer opens each calendar one by one.

reach.task: Confirm who will be on the unit that day
reach.learn: Which roles the free or busy view includes, and that it does not assign the shift

evidence.claim: A free or busy view can replace opening each calendar. It does not decide whether the skill mix or the equipment will work. Model knowledge.
Dutch works-council consent covers systems for rosters and staff data. This view shows free or busy for roles she already checks and does not score or assign staff. National rules vary.
Annex III point 4(b) covers evaluating or rostering staff on behaviour or traits. This view does not evaluate staff and does not set a roster.

assumptions: Staff already keep their own calendars. The view shows free or busy for the roles she names. It does not choose who works.
The study nurse keeps the equipment booking list. The coordinator does not, so focal incremental hours are 0. If equipment is not on that list, she determines it with the site lead.
The call with the site lead is a conversation inside the study team, not a message sent outside. The date note is written in the same study file.
unknowns: Whether the works council treats this free or busy view as monitoring of named staff.
research_questions: Does the works council treat this free or busy view as staff monitoring?

already_counted.description: Reading the named sites, judging equipment, arranging the date with the site lead, and recording it stay in her remaining time.

incremental.description: The study nurse keeps the equipment booking list.
The coordinator does not keep that booking list.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: One site and one colleague is a short calendar look, near 4. Several staff across dates can reach 10. Equipment conflicts and the conversation stay hers.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: She still organizes the study room, checks every recruitment claim before it goes out, calculates and dispenses each dose, and arranges the site. The lookups and the draft do not take those decisions.
skills_to_grow: Match each drafted sentence to an ethics-approved claim before release
Calculate a dose from the strength on screen, and stop when the field is missing
Read free or busy without treating it as a decision about who should work
Place equipment from the visit list when the cupboard note is wrong
role.ambitious_version: When the ethics text already covers the claims, she can prepare the recruitment wording in the same week and still check every sentence. She still organizes the room, calculates every dose, and arranges the site.
